title: The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy
author: ERAN YASHIV
text:
Carrie Shaltz/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images

The Economist’s Embarrassing Proxy War Over AI Policy

Aug 26, 2026

Eran Yashiv

The disagreements between the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu and his opponents are consequential—and so are the opponents. But rather than engage in good faith with Acemoglu's arguments, the venerable British news magazine recently stooped to bibulous calumny by unnamed critics of his work.

TEL AVIV—By publishing a recent article smearing the Nobel laureate economist Daron Acemoglu, The Economist has demonstrated bad judgment, overweening arrogance, and bad faith. The magazine engages with Acemoglu’s academic work disingenuously, quoting the snarky comments of unnamed economists interviewed over drinks to support its argument that his influential research makes sweeping, unfounded claims. Acemoglu’s research linking institutions to long-run prosperity—the work that the Nobel committee honored two years ago—supposedly is little better than glib. And Acemoglu’s pessimism about AI and his preference for steering technological change through public policy rest on dubious assumptions and underestimate AI’s potential economic benefits.
